title: Credit Card Spending Cashback · Project Delivery Flow
status: Project delivery and capability evolution flow

scenario.parent_requirement: Platinum card customers get an extra 0.5% cashback on their spending over the next 3 months.
scenario.slice: Platinum card customers get an extra 0.5% cashback on their spending over the next 3 months.
why: Platinum card customers, 3 months and an extra 0.5% are the current requirement scope.
Campaign dates, amount rounding and test inputs are verified against local flow parameters; the formal business rules still need confirmation.
This delivery's records and knowledge reference the current requirement and do not reuse check results from other campaigns.
scenario.seed: Platinum card customers · 3-month spending period · extra 0.5% cashback
scenario.roles: Project Owner and project member are Teams collaboration identities; the CardDemo administrator/cardholder are business acceptance case roles and are not mixed up with Teams permissions.

acceptance_criteria.expected: Platinum cards enter reward calculation and standard cards do not; the formal eligibility rules are to be confirmed.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Local rule checks CB-01, CB-02; formal service evidence pending.

acceptance_criteria.expected: Checked against the configured three-month window, start inclusive and end exclusive; formal dates are to be confirmed.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Local rule checks CB-03 to CB-05; formal service evidence pending.

acceptance_criteria.expected: CNY 120.00 earns an extra CNY 0.60 cashback, calculated in integer cents; other formal business rules are to be confirmed.

skill.name: dev-frontend-ui
skill.status: Candidate definition, published after Owner confirmation
skill.reason: The missing card eligibility rule let standard cards enter reward calculation.
changes: Add positive and negative rule checks for platinum and standard cards.
Cover the start and end boundaries of the three-month period.
Check the extra 0.5% and rounding in integer cents, and keep the duplicate-handling check.
evaluation: Platinum card CNY 120.00 earns CNY 0.60 cashback.
No cashback at the campaign end instant.
skill.comparison: The candidate definition is checked with fixed rule inputs; the external model comparison evaluation was not run.

agent.name: Code Agent
agent.status: Configuration candidate; the base model is unchanged
agent.reason: All acceptance rules must be checked independently before submission, so that coverage is not limited to positive inputs.
changes: Generate positive and negative checklists per acceptance item.
Save inputs, actual results and rule versions; do not present fixed records as real model runs.
Keep functional acceptance separate from production security release.
evaluation: Block submission when a rule is missing.
Keep the status as to be verified when the execution report is missing.
Once all seven rules pass, the work can go to functional acceptance; the security status stays unverified.
agent.comparison: Rule checks and model experiment status are saved separately; flow operations are not treated as real Agent experiments.

trace.join_rule: Requirement → Context → Check records → Fix → Retest → Acceptance; records come from a local workflow fixture and are not linked to native historical sessions.

gaps.name: Production security
gaps.fact: Real enterprise identity authentication and security scanning are not integrated.
gaps.limit: Functional acceptance is not production release.

gaps.name: Business rules
gaps.fact: Formal campaign dates, settlement, refund and limit rules still need confirmation.
gaps.demo: Only the explicitly listed local rule parameters are verified for now.
gaps.limit: Do not infer that undefined rules mean no limits in production.

gaps.name: Execution and evaluation
gaps.fact: The workflow uses fixed inputs and operation records; no external model, payment or native Agent is called.
gaps.demo: Source labels and an independent evaluation status are kept.
gaps.limit: Fixed records are not described as real historical runs.

records: Individual resources/sharing publish and subscription records/project adopted versions
invariants: Role switching shares one state; per-resource publishing controls market access and subscriptions, and existing project and user resources can be selected directly.
Capability adoption is explicitly bound to the work snapshot; upgrades do not rewrite earlier work.
A quality failure blocks the current delivery from passing; earlier failures remain viewable.
Security without a report stays unverified; a functional pass does not automatically become a production release.
Evaluation and publish are separate actions; a failed candidate can go back for revision.
Every record keeps its source type; fixed fixtures and real run results are stored separately.
